description: Drop Zone Support Team Leader relays surface wind and limited weather observations to the flight deck (Aircraft Commander) via the dz-safety-of-flight-radio-net — the actual first hop of the information path that ultimately reaches the Loadmaster relayed through the flight deck. This radio contact is limited to safety-of-flight matters (ATC directions, range clearance, unsafe surface conditions, mission changes) and wind/weather, not continuous chatter, and is mandatory (not just customary) for IMC/AWADS instrument drops.

description: Loadmaster rolls on, configures, and operates the Rapid Dragon-class deployment boxes for palletized ISR UAV airdrop — the roll-on/roll-off design requires no aircraft modification, per AFRL's public materials.

The specific loadmaster procedure for configuring/operating a Rapid Dragon-class pallet is not documented in any source found this session; the general roll-on/roll-off, no-modification design is confirmed, so a loadmaster-operated interaction is a reasonable structural inference, not a directly documented procedure.

description: TOC-L Coordinator coordinates UAV pallet deployment timing and configuration with the Loadmaster ahead of release — the C5ISR Airdrop mission's analogue to the DZSTL/Loadmaster coordination relationship in the CDS-resupply mission.

doctrineSource.publication: "Air Force TOC-L enhances joint force C2"
doctrineSource.note: Same verification status as the toc-l C2Node record's citation — the general TOC-L/aircraft C2 connection is real and documented; this specific coordination relationship is this mission's extension of it.

description: TOC-L Coordinator provides the Loadmaster detailed UAV flight-plan and launch-sequence instructions — which pallet/UAV launches in what order, at what point in the run, and any deployment-specific configuration — before the drop run begins. This is the specific information-flow the Loadmaster needs beyond the CDS-resupply mission's simpler rigging/release picture.

doctrineSource.publication: "Air Force TOC-L enhances joint force C2"
doctrineSource.note: Same verification status as the toc-l C2Node record's citation. TOC-L's real documented function is air-picture/sensor-fusion, not UAV flight-plan production specifically — this interaction is this mission's fictional extension, stated explicitly rather than presented as a documented TOC-L procedure.

description: Rapid Dragon-class deployment box airdrops and releases the long-endurance ISR/comms-relay UAVs, which then transition to powered flight and establish their sensor/communications network.

doctrineSource.publication: Air Force Research Laboratory, "Rapid Dragon" / "Palletized Effects"
doctrineSource.note: Same verification status as the two System records this interaction connects.

description: The deployed UAV network relays sensor and communications-relay data to the TOC-L, which fuses it into the common operating picture — the intelligence and C2 support this mission provides to the broader relief effort.

doctrineSource.publication: "Air Force TOC-L enhances joint force C2"
doctrineSource.note: TOC-L's real documented function is fusing sensor/battle-management feeds into a common picture; that it specifically receives feeds from airdropped ISR UAVs is this mission's extension, not independently documented.
